title: Review and UGC Insights for Product Teams
summary: Classify reviews, Q&A, social comments and return reasons into product issues by SKU and batch, including Hinglish text, and give product teams a weekly digest with source quotes.

seo.title: Review and UGC Insights for Product Teams | VipraTech
seo.description: AI classifies marketplace reviews, social comments and return reasons into product issues by SKU, handles Hinglish and flags emerging problems early.

problem.intro: Customers tell you what is wrong with your products every day, in marketplace reviews, Q&A, Instagram comments, support tickets and return reasons. The feedback is spread across channels, often in Hinglish or regional languages, and reaches the product team as an average star rating.

pain_points.title: Too much to read
pain_points.detail: Reviews and comments across marketplaces, your site and social channels outrun any team's ability to read them.

pain_points.title: Ratings hide reasons
pain_points.detail: A three-star rating could mean poor fit, late delivery or a damaged box, and only the text says which.

pain_points.title: Hinglish breaks keyword tools
pain_points.detail: Text like 'fitting thodi tight hai' or 'smell achha nahi' defeats sentiment tools built for English.

pain_points.title: Problems found late
pain_points.detail: A packaging defect or a bad batch shows up in returns weeks after the first reviews mentioned it.

solution.overview: We build an insights pipeline that collects reviews, Q&A, social comments, support tickets and return reasons from official seller exports, APIs and your own systems. An LLM classifies each item against your product taxonomy, such as size and fit, quality, packaging, delivery, fragrance or skin reaction, at the aspect level and in English, Hindi, Hinglish and regional languages. Mentions are linked to SKU and, where possible, batch or lot. Spike detection flags themes rising faster than usual for a SKU. Product and quality teams get a weekly digest with counts and representative quotes, and safety-related mentions go to quality at once.
capabilities: Collects reviews, Q&A, comments, tickets and return reasons from official exports, APIs and internal systems
Aspect-level classification against your taxonomy, in English, Hindi, Hinglish and regional languages
Links feedback to SKU, variant and, where available, batch or lot
Detects rising themes per SKU and alerts the owning team
Routes mentions of skin reactions, injuries or contamination to the quality team immediately
Weekly digest with counts, trends and representative quotes linked to the source

workflow.title: Collect feedback
workflow.detail: Reviews, Q&A, social comments, tickets and return reasons are pulled daily from approved sources.

workflow.title: Clean and link
workflow.detail: Personal details are stripped, and each item is linked to SKU, variant and batch where possible.

workflow.title: Classify by aspect
workflow.detail: The LLM tags each item with aspects and sentiment from your taxonomy, with a confidence score.

workflow.title: Detect safety mentions and spikes
workflow.detail: Safety-related mentions and unusual rises in a theme are flagged.

workflow.title: Human review
workflow.detail: Quality assesses safety mentions, and analysts check low-confidence items and approve taxonomy changes.

workflow.title: Publish insights
workflow.detail: Dashboards and a weekly digest go to product, quality and CX teams.

inputs: Marketplace reviews and Q&A from seller exports or APIs
Reviews and questions from your own site
Product taxonomy, SKU master and batch data
outputs: Aspect-level tags and sentiment per feedback item
Theme trends by SKU, variant, channel and batch
Safety mention alerts to the quality team
human_in_the_loop: The quality team assesses every safety-related mention, and analysts review low-confidence classifications and approve taxonomy changes. The system does not post public replies or contact reviewers.
integrations: Marketplace seller portals and review exports
Helpdesk such as Freshdesk or Zendesk
BI tools such as Power BI or Looker
guardrails: Data collected only through official exports, APIs or with platform permission
Every count links back to source quotes
Regular sampling of classifications against analyst labels
Safety mentions routed to people, never closed automatically
compliance_notes: Reviewer names and handles are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023 and are removed before analysis.
Collection follows each platform's terms of service.

pilot.scope: Reviews, tickets and return reasons for one category over the past two quarters, with the weekly digest running for the last two weeks of the pilot.
deliverables: Taxonomy agreed with product, quality and CX
Accuracy report against analyst-labelled samples, including Hinglish
Roll-out plan for other categories and channels

what_we_measure.how: Tags compared with analyst labels on a random sample, reported separately for English and for Hinglish or regional text.
Spikes and themes the product or quality team confirms as real issues.
Date a theme was flagged compared with when it appeared in return or complaint reports.
Time to prepare the weekly product feedback report, with and without the pipeline.

faqs.q: Can it read Hinglish and regional languages?
faqs.a: Yes. The classifier handles code-mixed and transliterated text, as well as Hindi and common regional languages. The pilot reports accuracy for these separately, so you can see where it is strong and where it needs review.
We use official seller exports, APIs or reports available to you as a seller, and follow each platform's terms. We do not scrape against terms of service.

faqs.q: Can it tell us which batch has a problem?
faqs.a: Only where batch or lot data can be linked, for example through order and dispatch records or return inspections. Without that link, it reports by SKU and date.

faqs.q: Does it write replies to reviews?
faqs.a: This system focuses on insights for product teams. Drafting replies is possible, but nothing is posted publicly without a person approving it.
